summary: Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held posts at Hampshire College (attested 2001) and Rollins College.

Mario Poceski works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. After earning his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. by 2000, he held visiting positions at Iowa, Komazawa, Stanford, NUS, Hamburg, and Fudan, and taught at the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Mario Praz (1896–1982) studied at the Universities of Bologna (~1914–1918) and Florence (~1918–1920). He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral research under supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, having also studied under Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer (born 1954) is a history and archaeology scholar. She held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (~1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (~2003).

Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning a PhD from Cambridge under K. R. Norman (~1989–1994). He served at SOAS (~1995–1998) and the University of Sydney, becoming an Associate Professor (~2010).

Mark Andrew Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and has held positions at UCLA, Samcheok National University, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Mark Csikszentmihalyi (born 1964) is a sinologist and philosopher. He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2007) before becoming Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at the University of California, Berkeley (~2007).

Mark D. Griffiths (born 1966) earned a BSc at Bradford and a PhD at Exeter (1988–1990). He held posts at the Workers' Educational Association, the University of Plymouth (1990–1995), and Nottingham Trent University as Professor of Gambling Studies (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott is a scholar in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He held a post as professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and was appointed Professor at Harvard University (~2003).

Mark I. Wallace (born 1956) is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Chicago under Paul Ricœur (1986). He held posts at Princeton Theological Seminary, Merrimack College, and Georgia State University, and serves as Professor of Religion at Swarthmore College.

Mark Jan Dresden (1911–1986) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Amsterdam and Utrecht, as well as under Jan Gonda, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Bruno Henning, before teaching Iranian languages at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).

Mark Juergensmeyer (born 1940) studied at Illinois, Union Theological Seminary, Columbia, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1974). A religious studies and Indology scholar, he held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College (~2017).

Mark L. Blum works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held posts at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006), and was appointed Professor at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center (attested 2026).
Mark Owen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Leeds under the doctoral supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Pedersen is a scholar of computational linguistics who earned his PhD at the University of Queensland by 2001 and held a post at the same institution.

Mark Rowe is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who has held academic posts at McMaster University, including Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2015, 2026).

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (1951–2025) studied Indology at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Oxford (PhD ~1975–1979 under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson), as well as with traditional teachers in India.

Mark Siderits (born 1946) is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Illinois State University (~1979–2007; Emeritus Professor ~2008) and served as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Seoul National University (~2008–2014).

Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Cambridge under Elizabeth De Michelis. He held a post as Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
